The UNCT-SWAP Gender Equality Scorecard is a United Nations system-wide accountability and self-assessment framework that enables United Nations Country Teams (UNCTs) to assess how effectively gender equality and women’s empowerment are mainstreamed across their collective work. The Scorecard assesses UNCT performance across seven dimensions and 15 Performance Indicators and supports Country Teams in identifying gaps and agreeing corrective actions to strengthen gender mainstreaming. UNCT Azerbaijan has implemented the UNCT-SWAP Gender Equality Scorecard through a comprehensive assessment followed by annual progress assessments, most recently in 2025. Preparatory work, including identification of IAT members and compilation of available evidence, has already commenced. The assessment will build on previous UNCT-SWAP findings and evidence and will result in a GEAP-aligned Action Plan reflecting relevant United Nations system-wide gender equality priorities. The final Comprehensive Report and Action Plan are to be submitted through the UNCT-SWAP reporting platform by 14 November 2026. In this context, UN Women Azerbaijan seeks to engage an International Consultant to provide technical guidance, analytical support and facilitation throughout the 2026 comprehensive UNCT-SWAP assessment. The consultant will facilitate the process in accordance with the 2023 UNCT-SWAP Gender Equality Scorecard Technical Guidance, while the IAT retains responsibility for providing and validating evidence, analysing performance and agreeing ratings and follow-up actions. We are recruiting seven roles across social science, sector, and technical expertise, and candidates may be considered for more than one. We anticipate that work will initially cover Fiji, Ecuador, and Bolivia but may expand to cover other countries. These positions are contingent on award of the contract. About The Opportunity MCC is an independent U.S. Government agency that promotes economic growth in poor countries with a demonstrated commitment to good governance. Its Social Analysis practice uses social science to improve program design, broaden impact, and reduce social risk. This technical directive supports MCC's work to strengthen partner countries' policy and regulatory environments for business, including registration, licensing, taxation, permitting, MSME and informal sector policy, foreign investment, and trade. The team will analyze the social and political economy dynamics that shape these reforms and identify barriers facing foreign investors, domestic firms, and emerging business owners. Work begins with programs in development in Fiji, Ecuador, and Bolivia, and MCC may add countries over the life of the contract. Areas of expertise We are recruiting in seven areas. Apply for every area you qualify for. The levels shown follow MCC's illustrative staffing for the directive; your level will depend on your years of experience. Area of expertise Labor category and level What you will do Political economy and business environment (lead) Social Scientist III Lead the analytical framing of how political, institutional, and social dynamics shape the business environment and the potential for reform. Oversee stakeholder analysis, incentive mapping, and distributional impact assessment across types of firms and business owners, and translate findings into policy guidance. Business environment and regulatory reform (lead) Sector Expert III Lead analysis of business enabling environment systems, including registration, licensing, taxation, permitting, trade policy, and foreign investment frameworks. Advise on reform priorities to improve competitiveness, reduce regulatory burdens, and strengthen institutional effectiveness. Regulatory reform implementation and institutional strengthening Technical Expert III Lead due diligence and advise on implementation strategies for regulatory reforms coordination across agencies, consistent enforcement, and reduced discretionary practices. Advise on institutional capacity building, monitoring systems, and sustaining reform outcomes. Enterprise impacts and institutional dynamics Social Scientist II Analyze how policies and regulations affect firms of different sizes, ownership structures, and levels of formality. Connect enterprise-level analysis to stakeholder incentives, coordination failures, and implementation constraints, using qualitative and quantitative data, including firm-level datasets. Institutional and organizational change Social Scientist II Analyze the social, cultural, and economic drivers that shape beliefs, practices, and decision-making at individual, enterprise, and institutional levels. Diagnose the norms and incentives that influence stakeholder responses and turn them into recommendations for program design. Trade, investment, and business regulation systems Sector Expert II Apply expertise in business regulation, trade policy, customs systems, and foreign investment frameworks. Analyze regulatory bottlenecks, administrative inefficiencies, and barriers to market entry and expansion, and recommend ways to streamline processes and improve policy coherence. Private sector development MSMEs, finance, and investment facilitation Technical Expert II Analyze constraints to business growth and formalization, including financing barriers, regulatory burdens, and weak support systems. Recommend ways to strengthen SME participation, improve access to capital, and attract and retain investment. Research Analyst Research Analyst II Conducts cross-cutting research and analysis on all aspects of this technical directive. Supports both technical and social workstreams through data collection, synthesis, and preparation of analytical outputs. Contributes to country diagnostics, comparative analysis, and reporting. Required Qualifications Candidates must meet the experience threshold for Level II or Level III Level II 10 to 14 years of experience in economic and social analysis, design, and/or implementation, and a bachelor's degree in a related field. Experience should include conducting social analysis and/or applying social analysis in project design or implementation in a relevant technical field. Level III 15 or more years of experience conducting social analysis and/or applying social analysis to the design and/or implementation of programs in developing countries, in relevant sectors. All candidates must have experience in the areas they apply for, gained in low-income and lower-middle-income countries. Each labor category also has its own requirement Social Scientist expertise in a social science (sociology, anthropology, demography, geography, economics, or community development) or a related discipline, and experience conducting social analysis, including stakeholder engagement. Sector Expert expertise in business policy and the regulatory environment, applied to the social analysis aspects of problem analysis, program design, and program implementation. Technical Expert experience applying a social analysis lens to a relevant technical area, such as political economy; legal, regulatory, policy, and institutional reform; entrepreneurship and employment; finance and access to markets; institutional and organizational change; or governance analysis and institutional capacity assessment. Preferred Qualifications Country or regional experience relevant to the current programs in Fiji, Ecuador, and Bolivia. Proficiency in more than one of English, Spanish, French, and Portuguese. Prior experience working with MCC. Qualifications in more than one of the areas of expertise listed above. How to apply Please upload your CV and a brief cover letter indicating, which position(s) you are applying for. These positions are contingent on [Company Name] being awarded the contract.

review_candidates.description: Position: Executive Driver & Security Detail Job type Full Time Category Administration Location / Branch University of Namibia / Main Campus Closing Date 23 October 2026 (2 weeks from now) Job Description Providing executive protection and secure transportation to the Vice-Chancellor, his/her top management, UNAM Council and external and international University guests during official travel, meetings, events and other authorised engagements. The position is responsible for assessing security risks, planning protective arrangements, conducting advance security activities, providing secure executive transportation, monitoring security information and responding to security and emergency situations, while maintaining a high level of confidentiality, discretion and professionalism. This position requires a 45-hour work week and availability for overtime, travel and after-hours duties, when required. Requirements Candidate must be in position of a Diploma in Police Science, Security Management, Security Training or related field, coupled with at least four (4) years’ relevant experience in executive protection, close protection, or a related environment. Candidate must have experience in executive/VIP protection and defensive driving, security risk assessment, advance security planning and emergency response. Candidate must have experience in dealing with senior executives, dignitaries, government officials or other high-profile stakeholders and preparing security incident reports. preference will be given to candidates with: Advanced Defensive Driving Certificate, Basic First Aid Certification, Public Driver’s Permit (PDP), Certificate of Good Conduct This position is subjected to security vetting.
